instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Half a season after a January move; raw, awkward and obviously athletic.
Twenty-four league goals leading the line for a title-challenging Arsenal; a genuinely elite season, and the only one of its kind he had.
Back to ten goals and a season of visible disinterest; the ability did not vanish but the level did.
Fourteen goals as a first-choice starter; the only season he sustained it.
A rotation option in his first English season, but the technique, the left foot and the finishing were already exceptional. Rated as the twenty-one-year-old he was, not the player he became.
Only fourteen starts before the ankle injury on international duty, but nine goals and seven assists in them; when fit he was unambiguously Arsenal’s best player.
Eighteen goals in nineteen starts once the ankle healed — the best finisher in the league over the second half of the season, on a third of a campaign.
Loan return after two injury-wrecked years at Atletico Madrid; used deeper and wider, and plainly short of the 1996/97 player.
Three seasons in Brazil in between and a serious knee injury behind him; nine starts back at Middlesbrough at 29, a long way from the 1996/97 player.
Eight goals in 26 starts and the creative centre of a League Cup-winning side; the sharpest he was after the injuries, still short of his peak.
An England cap at 21 and thirty starts in Derby’s midfield; the ability that made him a seven-million-pound player was real, whatever the fee came to represent.
Three starts - the knee and ankle injuries that wrecked his Leeds career.
Converted from centre-back to striker mid-season and thrived; athletic and quick.
Injuries and a stalled Blackburn move limited him to eight starts across both clubs.
Four years on from Crystal Palace, two of them outside the top flight; a 31-year-old utility defender in Bolton’s first season up.
Fringe at Arsenal at 21, but a genuine top-flight forward in the making; rated for the player he was then, not the Manchester City regular he became.
Six years on from four Arsenal appearances as a 21-year-old; a settled if limited Premier League forward by 27.
TargetMan rather than AerialThreat: a striker strong in the air, and AerialThreat at 3.5x on a ST decides the scoring charts by itself.
TargetMan rather than AerialThreat: a striker strong in the air, and AerialThreat at 3.5x on a ST decides the scoring charts by itself.
The Kevin Davies profile done slightly better: outstanding in the air, tireless in the press, a genuine top-flight centre-forward without the finishing to be more.
A capable, unspectacular deputy for Lehmann - sound handling, no command; comfortably below the modern standard.
Three years on from the deputy row above, and the best of his career: first choice for a side that led the title race into March.
Given three starts at 16, which is extraordinary; rated as the raw prospect he was that season, not the England keeper he became.
Ever-present for a fifth-placed Ipswich and called into the England squad. The 1994/95 row is three games by a 16-year-old six years earlier, so the rise is a career rather than a jump.
Twelve starts as understudy at Arsenal, with some conspicuous errors.
Seven starts before the double leg break in September 2000 that ended his career.
Three starts in a brief spell at Tottenham; he barely played top-flight football that season.

Scotland’s captain and a genuinely excellent passer and organiser; his Blackburn spell is remembered as a disappointment, which is a claim about the team and his fitness rather than about the footballer.
Thirty-one and an ever-present in Birmingham’s ninth-place season; still an excellent organiser and passer, with the legs going.
Nine goals in sixteen starts after the move; a prolific second-tier scorer who was ordinary in the top flight.
Nine goals in sixteen starts after the move; a prolific second-tier scorer who was ordinary in the top flight.
Ten starts; the knee and calf problems that ended his career at 28 had begun.
Four starts at 32; out of the Liverpool side rather than injured.
Seventeen and already physically a Premier League full-back - quick and composed on the ball; rated on that, not on the eleven starts.
Out of the side once City started buying, rather than any drop in what he could do.
Thirty-one and plainly slowing in his last Bolton season; the trickery survived, the influence did not.
His one outstanding season, first choice in a Blackburn side that finished sixth; the shooting from distance was a real weapon.
Four starts only; injury, not a drop in level.
Seven starts; the injuries that ended his career at 26, not a drop in level.
Rated on the player rather than the Spurs output: a Champions League-winning holding midfielder and Germany international, already past his physical peak at 28.
Twenty-one starts in a relegation season, at 30 and past his best. Note: the docs anchor puts his 1993/94 at 76 while the reviewed row here reads 73 — flagged, not changed.
